document_summary: Hoboken, NJ Code ch. 158 (Rent Increases): Article I requires disclosures for rent increases over 10% on lease renewal, and Article II prohibits algorithmic rent fixing by residential landlords.

rules.title: Algorithmic rent fixing in rental housing market prohibited
rules.requirement: Landlords of residential dwelling units in Hoboken may not price-fix using algorithmic pricing, meaning software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms that use nonpublic competitor information to coordinate, recommend or implement rents, lease terms or occupancy levels among competing lessors.
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic rent-fixing using nonpublic competitor information
rules.coverage_conditions: Any residential dwelling unit, defined as any primary residence, in the City of Hoboken. Nonpublic competitor information is information less than 365 days old that is not widely and readily available to the public at no cost.
rules.exemptions: Medical/long-term care and detention facilities are excluded from the definition of residential dwelling unit.
rules.interaction: New Jersey's FAIR Act (P.L. 2026, c.43) may preempt this ordinance once it takes effect. This capture does not address the FAIR Act.
rules.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.
rules.conflict_note: Open question: the NJ FAIR Act (P.L. 2026, c.43) may preempt this ordinance once effective. Not found in this capture; the document says nothing about the FAIR Act or preemption.
rules.extraction_notes: Month of adoption; exact effective date not stated in source (NJ ordinances generally take effect after final passage and publication). Adopted 7-9-2025 by Ord. No. B-781. Enforcement is by the Division of Housing or an aggrieved private citizen in Municipal Court.

rules.title: Mandatory disclosures for rental increases over 10%
rules.requirement: A landlord raising rent by more than 10% on lease renewal must give the tenant an itemization of costs, a statement on whether a rent algorithm was used, notice of the right to take legal action, and Division of Housing contact information. These go in the lease (on the first page) or on a Division of Housing form, before the increase takes effect.
rules.key_value: Disclosures required for renewal increases over 10%; no cap on the increase
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential landlords seeking to increase rent by more than 10% year over year upon renewal of a lease with a current tenant.
rules.quoted_span: All residential landlords seeking to increase rent by more than 10% upon a renewal of a lease with a current tenant year over year shall be required to make the following disclosures to existing tenants either in the lease upon renewal (must be clearly indicated on the first page) or on a form provided by the Hoboken Division of Housing prior to the increase being implemented:

This is a disclosure/notice duty, not a cap on rent increases; it is filed under rent_increase_limits as the closest category.
